rulings.barItem: vendor behaviour the vendor's documentation contradicts
rulings.reason: Act 3 (Who can reply: Following, the game-dev community note) and act 6 (Made with AI) tell three submissions that end in 'the twin reports its gap' and 'remains unsent'. X documents reply_settings "following", community_id with share_with_followers, and made_with_ai as valid fields of POST /2/tweets (the vendored X API v2 document 2.168, CreatePostsRequest; https://docs.x.com/changelog, 28 Jul 2025, community posts shared with followers). On X each of these posts is published. The outline admits these are twin limitations, so the story it tells is not the customer's year on X.
rulings.correction: Tell each of the three as X answers it (the devlog published to followers-only replies, the community note sent, the AI-disclosed recording post published), or remove them from acts 3 and 6.

steps: What the life does not do
rulings.barItem: vendor behaviour the vendor's documentation contradicts
rulings.reason: The closing paragraph says the auto-plug reply 'meets its likes threshold but is refused by the documented self-serve summons rule'. The auto-plug replies to Volter's own devlog post. X's rule (https://docs.x.com/x-api/posts/manage-tweets/introduction; https://docs.x.com/changelog, 23 Feb 2026) concerns replies to another author's post, and X's developer forum (https://devcommunity.x.com/t/restricting-programmatic-replies-does-this-affect-replying-to-itself/257955) answers that replying to your own post is unaffected.
rulings.correction: Tell the auto-plug reply as published under the devlog post.

steps: What the life does not do
rulings.barItem: a stated cause that never happens, and a promise never kept
rulings.reason: Act 4 has Mira reply with a question and the closing paragraph has Mira's account protected, with Ines following the reply to its privacy notice. Volter never follows Mira. X's Help Center (https://help.x.com/en/safety-and-security/public-and-protected-posts) states that replies a protected account sends to an account not following it will not be seen by that account, so Volter never learns of the question.
rulings.correction: Make Mira's account public and drop Ines's visit to the protected reply.

steps: What the life does not do
rulings.barItem: a state switched away and back in one sitting, or returned with no reason the story shows
rulings.reason: The closing paragraph adds 'her later channel reconnection uses Sign in with X's remembered approval, and an old consent tab is invalid'. Nothing in the acts disconnects the channel, and X's OAuth 1.0a access tokens 'do not expire but can be revoked by the user at any time' (https://docs.x.com/fundamentals/authentication/oauth-1-0a/obtaining-user-access-tokens). The reconnection and the stale tab have no cause in the story.
rulings.correction: Remove the reconnection and the old consent tab from the outline.

rulings.barItem: a stated cause that never happens, and a promise never kept
rulings.reason: Act 5 has Ines 'credit Mira in her next draft', with three searches (the display name, the handle, then 'a subsequent typo' after she has already found Mira). The draft is never posted, and no later Scheduler post mentions @mira_builds (the 15 June post is the recording). Mira is also an audience member who asked about Linux, not an artist owed credit. The third search, after the find, is a tour of the lookup's not-found answer.
rulings.correction: Drop the typo search after the find, and either publish the draft that mentions @mira_builds (for answering the devlog) or drop the mention from act 5.

steps: What the life does not do
rulings.barItem: a refusal without a cause the story shows, or the same cause drawn twice; a run of refusals
rulings.reason: One verification sitting fails twice on the same cause, Volter's unfinished Dub-for-X setup: a preview callback left in X's developer console (closing paragraph) and 'percent-marked placeholder client keys' in the deployment (act 9). The second has no cause the story shows. Its literal '%' exists to reach RFC 6749's malformed-credential branch, which X's token page (https://docs.x.com/fundamentals/authentication/oauth-2-0/user-access-token) does not describe.
rulings.correction: Keep the preview-callback mismatch and its correction, and drop the placeholder-key failure, the half-hour wait and the second consent from act 9.
